prompt: Many companies sponsor sports as a way of advertising themselves. Some people think this is good for the world of sport, while others think it is negative. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Many people believe that companies sponsor sports for their commercial purposes, and this is positive. While others regard it as negative. This essay will discuss both views before offering a reasoned opinion.

Firstly, proponents of sponsorship believe that sponsoring sports can have a positive impact on sports. When companies sponsor sports, they provide financial support for sporting events, which provides event organizers with adequate financial resources. This can also lead to increased visibility and popularity of sports, making them attract large groups or live audiences. This sparks passion in many young people to become athletes, and the sponsorship provides them with opportunities to excel.

On the other hand, critics argue that sponsorship has negative impacts that companies are fully aware of. Sports have become more commercialized than a fair game or community event. Sponsors are more focused on making money rather than supporting sports. They know about the emotional connections fans have with sports. Fans deeply admire their favourite athletes and teams. When a brand supports those teams, fans transfer their positive feelings and loyalty from the sport to the company. Sponsorship has also affected athletes' performance. Companies that pay money to athletes, teams, or events have developed a mindset of winning at all costs, where they are willing to sacrifice fair play, ethics, health, and safety. For instance, many athletes cheat, intentionally injure opponents, and use performance-enhancing drugs to win just to receive massive financial rewards and salaries. They play through severe concussions or serious injuries for prize pools.

In my opinion, sponsorship is somewhat beneficial for encouraging sports but can be detrimental for professional athletes, as it can cause serious harm to their mental and physical health, leaving them with less potential to participate in sports further.
